## 3. The designed families as built

- **F-D1 FAST-CLOSE** — last 1800s of every phase run + the settlement window [RTH_HI-1800s, RTH_HI); delays [15, 60]
- **F-D2 MICRO-OPENS** — micro-opens ['TOKYO_LUNCH_REOPEN', 'NY_CASH_OPEN']; 300s window, 15s delay
- **F-D3 NEWS-WINDOW** — first 600s after FOMC 14:00 ET (meeting last day) and the fixed 08:30/10:00 ET slots; delays [15, 60]; BOJ unavailable pre-2026
- **F-D4 POST-SHOCK** — first confirmation strictly after a causal shock episode ends: trailing-150s SANE mid range >= $1000, or a run of >= 10s wide-but-two-sided (D-054 insane) seconds; delay tau*
- **F-D5 FIRST-TEST** — earliest confirming touch per (session, kept level family); touch_count==1 carried as the VIRGIN sub-tag; delay tau*
- **F-D6 EXHAUSTION-AT-EXTENSION** — entry mid beyond an OR_EXT k>=1.5 level (adopted CC-M1-6.1 cells; FD6_ANY = all segment x OR-minute cells); delay tau*

Event supply over all 4073 sessions: 4613 causal repricing episodes + 1204 wide-book episodes -> 6268 F-D4 triggers (`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/session_context.tsv`).

## 7. Adoption recommendation (what this lane would take forward)

The CC-M1-3.2 metric is an OR of three tests, and two of them are degenerate for this stage — that is a finding, not an excuse:

- (ii) MARGINAL RECALL is saturated: the frozen union roster already captures 0.9966 of 1468 SI gate legs, so no added family can move recall by the +0.2pp the metric asks for [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/recall_variants.tsv:5`].
- (ii) MARGINAL RECALL is saturated: the frozen union roster already captures 0.9979 of 969 HG gate legs, so no added family can move recall by the +0.2pp the metric asks for [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/recall_variants.tsv:26`].
- (ii) MARGINAL RECALL is saturated: the frozen union roster already captures 0.9969 of 1272 NKD gate legs, so no added family can move recall by the +0.2pp the metric asks for [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/recall_variants.tsv:47`].
- (iii) DP SEAT SHARE rewards SIZE, not quality: a tag covering a third of the roster inherits a third of the seats at exactly baseline value. F-D6 is the case in point below.
- (i) CONDITIONAL VALUE is therefore the operative test here, and the honest reading adds a second requirement the metric does not state: the family must be SMALLER and BETTER than the baseline, not merely not-worse.

**THE HORIZON CONFOUND (this lane's most important caveat).** The CC-M1-3.2 value is the walled PHASE-CLOSE certificate, and its horizon is the time from the decision to that close — which is a function of the clock. Any family or slice defined ON the clock therefore measures edge AND horizon together. Both halves of §10 are cut on the clock, so every table below carries the walled PEAK-exit certificate beside it as the horizon-free comparator (`conditional_value_peak_usd` in `artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/family_value.tsv`, `value_peak_exit_usd` + `median_horizon_to_phase_close_sec` in `artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/slice_census.tsv`). Where the two disagree, the disagreement IS the result:

- F-D1 FAST-CLOSE loses -667 / -376 / -455 (SI/HG/NKD) on the close certificate but only +22 / +44 / -99 on the peak-exit one: its deficit is an EXIT-HORIZON effect, not a signal-quality effect. The candidates move; the certificate just closes the position before they finish.
- F-D2 and F-D3 are the mirror image: strong on the close certificate (+$294 / +$460 SI) and ~flat on the peak-exit one (+12 / +29), i.e. much of their measured edge is 'entered with the phase still ahead of it', not 'opens and releases are special'.
- F-D4 POST-SHOCK and F-D5 FIRST-TEST are the two that survive BOTH readings (F-D4 +423 / +363 / +526 peak-exit vs G1; F-D5 +208 / +188 / +168) — they are the genuine mechanism finds of this stage.

| family | reading | recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-D3 NEWS-WINDOW | +$460 SI / +$222 NKD / +$184 HG at n=21229/9467/13831 FIT, sign-stable in all four FIT years, 2025 echo higher — but ~flat on the horizon-free comparator | **ADOPT** on the operative (close-exit) metric, which is also the contract's hold-to-close shape (D-019); 15s and 60s land within $7 of each other, so one delay suffices |
| F-D4 POST-SHOCK | the largest per-candidate edge of the stage (+$744 SI / +$749 NKD / +$375 HG) on the smallest supply (n=464/911/111 FIT), era-concentrated, and it SURVIVES the horizon-free comparator | **ADOPT — the strongest find of the stage**, with the small-sample caveat |
| F-D2 MICRO-OPENS | consistent positive edge (+$294 / +$80 / +$84) at n=6076/5651/4323 FIT, ~flat peak-exit | **ADOPT** on the close-exit metric, with the horizon caveat |
| F-D5 FIRST-TEST | close-exit is asset-split ($133 NKD / $-185 SI / $-8 HG) but PEAK-exit is positive on all three ($+168 / $+208 / $+188): the first test of a level is a real quality signal that the close certificate under-reads | **ADOPT on NKD**; on SI/HG adopt as a FEATURE now and re-test as a family once an exit rule exists |
| F-D6 EXHAUSTION | passes only on size: 189953 SI candidates at $7 vs G1, and HG adopted no OR_EXT cell so the family is empty there | **DO NOT adopt as a generator family** — it emits no new candidate and has no value edge; keep the beyond-extension flag as a FEATURE |
| F-D1 FAST-CLOSE | decisively negative on the close certificate ($-667 SI / $-455 NKD / $-376 HG) but essentially AT baseline on the peak-exit one ($+22 / $-99 / $+44) | **RETIRE as a generator family** under the phase-close exit, and HAND THE FINDING TO THE EXIT PROGRAM (D-045/D-046): these candidates are not bad, they are cut off — a hold-through-the-boundary exit is the experiment |

SLICE MINER: the promotion bar the spec sets (G1 + $150) is LOW against these rosters — G1 is the weakest of the five S1-v2 families, so 13-17% of all tested cells clear it (`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/slice_multiplicity.tsv`). The operative output is therefore the RANKED top-20 per asset (§5) plus one structural finding that repeats on every asset and every axis pairing: value concentrates in a narrow CLOCK band interacted with the HIGH vol-regime tercile (SI/HG: UTC 11:00-13:00, the London-NY overlap; NKD: UTC 22:00-23:30 and 04:30, the Tokyo open and the Japan afternoon), plus a day-of-week tilt (Thu/Fri on SI/HG, Mon on NKD). CAUTION, stated because it matters for deployment: `spread_state=WIDE` cells rank high on SI and NKD, and those are exactly the seconds the m0 tradability screen (spread <= 2x phase median) rejects — that value may not be capturable, and the pair should be re-measured on the screened roster before any of it becomes a family. SECOND CAUTION, from the horizon confound above: the winning clock cells also carry the LONGEST median horizon to the phase close, so `value_peak_exit_usd` is the column to read before any clock slice is promoted to a family.

## 8. Spec defects returned to the orchestrator

- **FD-1** F-D1 'the settlement window' is undefined in the spec and no exchange settlement time is pinned anywhere in the repo. PINNED: the last 1800s before the committed m0 RTH close (RTH_HI_SEC = 21:00 UTC, common.py:104). If the orchestrator means the true COMEX/CME settlement periods, they must be pinned as constants. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:5`]
- **FD-2** F-D3's BOJ leg is not buildable: calendar_boj.csv carries 2026+ only (SOURCES_FOR_PORT.md:32) and BOJ decisions have no fixed release minute (day-grain flag). F-D3 ran on FOMC + the fixed 08:30/10:00 ET slots; the BOJ sub-window is DEFERRED with a revisit hook (D-015), not dropped. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:6`]
- **FD-3** F-D2 'London-NY handoff minute' is ambiguous: the frozen phase table already opens NY at the London/NY profile boundary, so the handoff as a MICRO-open (beyond the 3 phases) is pinned to the US cash open 09:30 ET. If the intent was the phase boundary itself, that window is already G1-FAST-OPEN. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:7`]
- **FD-4** F-D4 has no stated episode-size or trigger-latency bound. PINNED: causal detectors (trailing-150s $1000 repricing; >=10s insane run) and the first confirmation strictly after the episode, same session, no latency cap (the latency distribution is reported). [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:8`]
- **FD-5** §10B names 'selected 2-way cells' without a selection rule. PINNED: ALL 2-way axis pairs, with the pre-registered n>=500 FIT filter doing the selecting; every tested cell enters the Holm ledger, so the accounting stays honest. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:9`]
- **FD-6** §10B names no significance test. PINNED: one-sided Welch z on the conditional (positive-certificate) values, slice vs complement, normal tail; n>=500 makes the normal approximation safe. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:10`]
- **FD-8** METRIC DEFECT (found by this lane, returned for adjudication): the CC-M1-3.2 conditional value is measured on the walled PHASE-CLOSE certificate, whose horizon is a function of the clock, while §10's designed families and slice axes are cut ON the clock. Value and horizon are therefore confounded in the adoption metric itself. This lane reports the walled PEAK-exit certificate beside every number as the horizon-free comparator; the orchestrator should decide whether adoption uses the close-exit metric (the D-019 contract shape), the horizon-free one, or a horizon-normalised value. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:11`]
- **FD-7** STALE SPEC PIN (returned, not touched by this lane): commit d761a30 amended design/PORT_M1B_SPEC.md to sha16 d31f48b59877e44d but m1_common.py:42 still pins 2b83f9e70340a413, so verify_spec_m1b() raises today — b8_generation_v2.py, b7_sane.py, b7_levels_v2.py and hl_census.py cannot be re-run as committed. This is exactly the CC-M1-6.4 standing note. §10 pins the M1.A spec (its own home) and records the observed M1.B sha in the receipt instead. [`artifacts/cache/port/m1/family_discovery/spec_defects.tsv:12`]
